mainTopic: רבי's method of reading פסוקים and the שבועות ruling, the sources for ידיעה בתחילה ובסוף, and why our משנה counts the carrying cases of שבת as 'two that are four.'
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: why does רבי read the firstborn פסוקים as ריבוי ומיעוט when he usually uses כלל ופרט? The answer is that two general terms placed before the detail make the passage ריבוי ומיעוט, as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught about במים. The רבנן instead imagine the detail between the two general terms and read the passage as כלל ופרט. Since רבי normally uses כלל ופרט, the גמרא concludes that he wrote the שבועות ruling following רבי עקיבא. Next the גמרא studies the ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא and רבי disagree about how to learn ידיעה בתחילה and ידיעה בסוף from ״ונעלם״. רבא explains the wording, אביי rejects his explanation from סוטה and from a פסוק about the תורה, and אביי concludes that רבי counts ידיעת בית רבו as knowing. Finally, the גמרא asks why our משנה lists the carrying cases of שבת as only 'two that are four.' After one answer is rejected, רב פפא and רב אשי explain that the four are liable cases of carrying out and bringing in. The proof for רב אשי's claim continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the question on רבי's method
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the question started just before: why does רבי read these פסוקים with ריבוי ומיעוט when he normally uses כלל ופרט?
steps.simpleTranslation: …does רבי really expound using amplifications and restrictions?
steps.whatsHappening: These two words are the last words of a challenge that began just before this point. The גמרא is surprised that רבי reads the firstborn פסוקים using ריבוי ומיעוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different ways to read a general word followed by a specific word. With כלל ופרט, the law covers only what the detail names. With ריבוי ומיעוט, the law covers almost everything and leaves out only a little. The challenge is that רבי is known for using כלל ופרט, so his use of ריבוי ומיעוט here seems out of character.

keyTerms.meaning: Amplifications and restrictions. A broad word includes almost everything, and a later word removes only a little.
Generalizations and details. A general word followed by a detail means only the detail is included.

steps.confusionAlert: These two methods can give very different results from the same פסוק. Under כלל ופרט the law becomes narrow. Under ריבוי ומיעוט it becomes wide.

phrases.english: amplifications and restrictions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun before this point.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's use of ריבוי ומיעוט for the firstborn פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי normally expounds כלל ופרט, so using ריבוי ומיעוט here looks inconsistent.

steps.title: Usually כלל ופרט, but here a special reason applies
steps.stepSummary: Yes, רבי normally uses כלל ופרט. Here he switches because of a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, in general רבי expounds generalizations and details. But here, this is the reason he does not: he follows what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer agrees that רבי usually uses כלל ופרט. It then says this case is different, and it points to a source that will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody is changing what we know about רבי's general method. The answer says this pattern of פסוק is special. When two general words come first and the detail only afterward, the order makes it ריבוי ומיעוט and not כלל ופרט.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, usually
This is the reason
A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Yes, in general he expounds generalizations and details;
but here, this is the reason:
as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: a special word order changes which method applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי is inconsistent, since he uses כלל ופרט everywhere else.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי is consistent. Two general words placed before the detail make the passage ריבוי ומיעוט.

steps.title: The fish פסוק: במים written twice
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that when במים appears twice before the detail, the passage is read as ריבוי ומיעוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'in the water,' 'in the water,' written twice. This is not a generalization and a detail. It is an amplification and a restriction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source mentioned in step 2. It is a teaching about the פסוק that tells which fish we may eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fish פסוק, the general word במים comes twice, and only after that come the details, seas and rivers. The school of רבי ישמעאל says this pattern is ריבוי ומיעוט. The same pattern appears in the firstborn פסוקים: two general terms, then a detail. So רבי reads them the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: In the water. This is the general word in the fish פסוק.
It amplified and then restricted

phrases.english: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
'In the water,' 'in the water,' two times:
this is not a generalization and a detail,
but rather an amplification and a restriction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that step 2 relied on.
steps.raayaObject: Two general terms followed by a detail are read as ריבוי ומיעוט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל on במים במים.
steps.whatToRemember: A doubled general term that comes before the detail turns the reading into ריבוי ומיעוט. This is why רבי uses that method for the firstborn.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן still read the firstborn פסוקים as כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: Having explained רבי, the גמרא now turns to the רבנן. This one word sets up the next step, which gives their reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two general terms before a detail mean ריבוי ומיעוט, the רבנן need to explain why they still use כלל ופרט here. The question asks how they deal with the doubled general term.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי

phrases.english: And the רבנן?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how do they read this as כלל ופרט, given that two general terms come first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי to explaining the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רבנן read the passage as כלל ופרט despite the doubled general term.

steps.title: רבינא: put the detail between the two general terms
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a rule from ארץ ישראל: when two general terms sit next to each other, imagine the detail placed between them and read the passage as כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: as they say in the West, wherever you find two general terms next to each other, place the detail between them and judge them as a generalization and a detail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers for the רבנן. He uses a rule taught in ארץ ישראל that turns the doubled general term back into a כלל ופרט reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not let the order of the words decide the method. They mentally move the detail so it stands between the two general terms. That gives a general term, then a detail, then a general term, and the passage is judged by the כלל ופרט method. So the two sides disagree about whether the order of words in the פסוק matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Next to each other
Place, put
And judge them, read them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: two general terms before a detail mean ריבוי ומיעוט. רבנן: put the detail between them and read it as כלל ופרט.
steps.confusionAlert: Nobody actually changes the wording of the פסוק. 'Placing the detail between' is only a way of reading the פסוק.

phrases.english: רבינא said: as they say in the West:
Wherever you find
two general terms next to each other,
place the detail between them,
and judge them as a generalization and a detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the רבנן in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן follow the rule from ארץ ישראל: imagine the detail between the two general terms and read the passage as כלל ופרט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the dispute between רבי and the רבנן is about method: whether a doubled general term placed before the detail changes how the פסוק is read.

steps.title: If רבי uses כלל ופרט, the ruling on oaths is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: since רבי expounds with כללי ופרטי, the משנה's ruling on שבועות, which comes from ריבוי ומיעוט, cannot be his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said רבי expounds with generalizations and details, you have no choice: the ruling about oaths is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question it began earlier. It points out that the משנה's ruling on שבועות no longer fits רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 confirmed that רבי normally reads פסוקים as כלל ופרט, and uses ריבוי ומיעוט for the firstborn only because of the special word order. The שבועות ruling depends on reading the פסוק as ריבוי ומיעוט. So the claim that this משנה is רבי's own opinion is now under attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have said
Against your will, meaning you have no choice
Generalizations and details, the כלל ופרט method

phrases.english: Now that you said
that רבי expounds generalizations and details,
you have no choice: oaths is difficult!
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's ruling on oaths, which is learned through ריבוי ומיעוט.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of steps 2 to 5, that רבי expounds with כלל ופרט, to bring back the original challenge against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's ruling on שבועות is רבי's own view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שבועות ruling needs ריבוי ומיעוט, and רבי expounds with כלל ופרט, so the ruling cannot be his.

steps.title: רבי wrote the oaths ruling following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The answer: for שבועות, רבי wrote the משנה following רבי עקיבא's opinion, but he does not personally agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for oaths he wrote it according to רבי עקיבא, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In the part about שבועות, רבי wrote down רבי עקיבא's view and not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that the whole משנה shows רבי's own view is narrowed. The שבועות part follows רבי עקיבא, who does expound with ריבוי ומיעוט. This removes the contradiction with רבי's normal method.

keyTerms.meaning: He took or formulated, meaning he wrote the משנה this way
According to the view of
He does not hold this

steps.confusionAlert: רבי sometimes wrote a משנה following another תנא's opinion. A ruling in the משנה is not always רבי's personal view.

phrases.english: Rather, regarding oaths he formulated it
according to רבי עקיבא,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּעוֹת נָסֵיב אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the ruling to another תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שבועות ruling in the משנה is רבי's own opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי wrote the שבועות ruling following רבי עקיבא, but he does not hold that way himself.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns awareness at the start and end from the double ״ונעלם״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא. רבי עקיבא learns from ״ונעלם״ appearing twice that a person is liable only if he knew at the start, forgot in the middle, and knew again at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: From where do we know that one is liable only when there was awareness at the beginning, awareness at the end, and a lapse in between? The verse says ״ונעלם״ ״ונעלם״, two times. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies the ברייתא it quoted earlier, starting with רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be liable for entering the מקדש while טמא, the person must have known at first, then forgotten, then found out again. רבי עקיבא learns this from the word ״ונעלם״ written twice. The extra mention teaches the need for awareness before the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself, used to go back and study a source quoted earlier
Awareness at the beginning, before the sin
Awareness at the end, after the sin
A lapse of awareness in between, during the sin
And it was hidden, meaning he forgot

phrases.english: The matter itself:
From where do we know that he is liable only
for a case that has awareness at the beginning
and awareness at the end, and a lapse in between?
The verse says: "and it was hidden," "and it was hidden,"
two times. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section that studies the ברייתא quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One is liable only with ידיעה בתחילה, ידיעה בסוף, and העלם in between. רבי עקיבא learns this from ״ונעלם״ written twice.

steps.title: רבי finds both awarenesses elsewhere and uses the extra ״ונעלם״ for the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the double ״ונעלם״ is not needed for this. ״ונעלם״ itself shows he knew before, and ״והוא ידע״ shows he knew after. The extra ״ונעלם״ makes a person liable for forgetting the טומאה and also for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: That is not needed. The verse says ״ונעלם״, which shows he once knew, and ״והוא ידע״, so here are two awarenesses. If so, why does the verse say ״ונעלם״ again? To make him liable for forgetting the טומאה and for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives another way to learn the same rule. That frees the second ״ונעלם״ to teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, both ידיעות come from the wording: ״ונעלם״ means something he once knew got hidden, and ״והוא ידע״ is the awareness at the end. So the double ״ונעלם״ teaches that forgetting the מקדש also makes one liable, not only forgetting the טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed
From this we can tell that he knew
Forgetting that he was טמא
Forgetting that the place was the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, for רבי, a person who knew he was טמא but forgot he was in the מקדש is also liable.

phrases.english: רבי says: It is not needed,
for it says "and it was hidden"—
which shows that he knew,
and "and he knew"—
so here there are two awarenesses.
If so, why does the verse say "and it was hidden"?
To make him liable for forgetting the impurity
and for forgetting the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's source and gives a different reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both ידיעות come from ״ונעלם״ and ״והוא ידע״. The double ״ונעלם״ makes a person liable for forgetting the טומאה and for forgetting the מקדש.

steps.title: How does ״ונעלם״ show he once knew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי's claim from the ברייתא and asks how ״ונעלם״ shows earlier awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: ״ונעלם״ shows that he knew. How is that implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up one claim from רבי's words and asks for its source in the wording. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's whole reading depends on ״ונעלם״ meaning he knew before. The גמרא wants to see where in the word this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this implied?

phrases.english: The Master said: "and it was hidden"—
shows that he knew.
How is that implied?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר וְנֶעְלַם מִכְּלָל שֶׁיָּדַע מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind one claim in רבי's statement in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the word ״ונעלם״ do we see that the person knew before?

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק did not say ״והיא עלומה ממנו״
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that if the person never knew, the תורה would have written ״והיא עלומה ממנו״. Writing ״ונעלם״, which means it became hidden, shows he knew before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because it does not say ״והיא עלומה ממנו״.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The exact word the תורה chose shows that the person once knew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״עלומה ממנו״ would mean the thing was always hidden from him. ״ונעלם″ means it became hidden, so there must have been knowledge before. This supports רבי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is not written
Hidden from him, meaning it was never known to him

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's point: ״ונעלם״ (it became hidden) suggests earlier knowing, while ״והיא עלומה ממנו״ would mean it was never known. The next steps show that אביי challenges this reading and replaces it.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Since it is not written "and it is hidden from him."
phrases.notes: That wording would fit a person who never knew at all. ״ונעלם״ means it became hidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא מִדְּלָא כְּתִיב וְהִיא עֲלוּמָה מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה wrote ״ונעלם״ (it became hidden) and not ״והיא עלומה ממנו״ (it was always hidden), so the person must have known before.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the case of a suspected wife
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if ״ונעלם״ always means someone knew first, then the פסוק about a סוטה would mean her husband knew. But if he had known, the bitter waters would not work on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, then by סוטה, where it says 'and it was hidden from the eyes of her husband,' does that mean he knew at first? If he had known, would the waters test her?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation from step 11. He brings another פסוק that uses the same word ״ונעלם״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said ״ונעלם״ means 'it became hidden,' so there was earlier knowing. אביי points out that the סוטה פסוק uses the same word, but there we cannot say the husband knew. If he had known, the bitter waters would not test her. So ״ונעלם״ does not have to mean earlier knowing.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife suspected of being unfaithful, who is tested with the bitter waters
But if that is so: introduces a challenge that pushes the other side's logic too far
By implication, which means 'does that show that...'
The waters test her (the bitter waters of the סוטה)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if that is so,
regarding a suspected wife, where it is written:
"and it was hidden from the eyes of her husband"
does that imply that he knew at first?!
If he had known,
would the waters test her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that ״ונעלם״ proves earlier knowing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears by סוטה, where earlier knowing by the husband is impossible, so the word cannot prove earlier knowing.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the husband could not have known
steps.stepSummary: אביי backs up his point with a ברייתא. The waters test the wife only when the husband is clean of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: 'And the man will be clean of sin, and that woman will bear her sin.' When the man is clean of sin, the waters test his wife. When the man is not clean of sin, the waters do not test his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to prove what he said in step 12: if the husband knew, the waters would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the waters only work when the husband has no sin. A husband who knew his wife sinned and stayed with her is not free of sin. So by סוטה, ״ונעלם״ must be used even though he never knew.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught (in a ברייתא)? Brings a source
Clean of sin
Test or check

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
"And the man will be clean of sin,
and that woman will bear her sin"
when the man is clean of sin,
the waters test his wife;
when the man is not clean of sin,
the waters do not test his wife!
phrases.notes: A husband who knew his wife sinned and stayed with her would not count as clean of sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of step 12
steps.raayaObject: That the husband of a סוטה could not have known earlier

steps.title: A second challenge from the hiddenness of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second challenge. The פסוק says the תורה 'was hidden' (״ונעלמה״) from all living things, yet another פסוק says no man ever knew its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, about the תורה it is written: 'And it was hidden from the eyes of all living, and from the birds of the sky it was concealed.' Does that imply someone knew it? But it is written: 'No man knows its value'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second example against רבא. Here too the word 'hidden' is used even though nobody knew the thing before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״ונעלם״ always means 'knew and then forgot,' then someone once knew the תורה fully. But another פסוק in איוב says no person ever knew its value. So this word can describe something that was never known at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: adds another challenge
And it was hidden
Its value or worth

phrases.english: And furthermore, regarding the Torah, where it is written:
"And it was hidden from the eyes of all living things,
and from the birds of the sky it was concealed"
does that imply there was someone who knew it?
But is it not written:
"No man knows its value"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second attack on רבא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that ״ונעלם״ proves earlier knowing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'hidden' is used for the תורה, which no person ever knew, so the word cannot prove earlier knowing.

steps.title: אביי: knowledge from one's teacher counts as knowing
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives his own explanation of רבי. Knowledge a person learned from his teacher as a child counts as 'knowing,' so ״ונעלם״ can refer to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: רבי holds that knowledge from one's teacher's house is called knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבא's reading, אביי offers a new way to understand how רבי finds earlier knowing in ״ונעלם״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person knew he touched something טמא. He also learned as a child that touching it makes a person טמא, even if he never put the two together. רבי counts that school learning as real knowing. So ״ונעלם״ fits: he 'knew,' and then it slipped from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowledge learned in one's teacher's house (basic school learning)
Is called knowledge, meaning it counts as knowing
He holds (this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי holds that what a person learned from his teacher counts as 'knowing.' That is how ״ונעלם״ can point to earlier knowledge, without saying the word itself always means 'knew first.'
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the person consciously knew 'I am טמא.' He means the person knew the facts and had learned the rule as a child, and that is enough to count as knowing.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Rabbi holds
knowledge from his teacher's house is called knowledge.
phrases.notes: He means the rules of טומאה a person learned as a child in school.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new explanation of רבי
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what counts as 'knowing'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא: the word ״ונעלם״ itself proves conscious earlier knowledge
steps.terutzMaskana: Earlier 'knowing' for רבי includes what a person learned from his teacher, combined with knowing he touched the טומאה

steps.title: רב פפא asks whether anyone lacks childhood knowledge
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: if learning from one's teacher counts as knowing, then the משנה's case of 'no awareness at the beginning' could never happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But what about the case in the משנה of 'no awareness at the beginning, but awareness at the end'? Is there anyone who does not have the basic knowledge he learned in his teacher's school?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks אביי's answer from step 15. He points to a case in the משנה that seems impossible under אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that knowledge learned as a child counts as 'knowing.' But the משנה mentions a person who had no knowledge at the beginning at all. Since every Jew learns the basics as a child, רב פפא asks how such a person could exist.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness at the beginning, before the sin happened
Awareness at the end, after the sin happened
Knowledge a person learned from his teacher, usually as a child
Is there anyone? A question that expects the answer 'no'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But that which is taught
"there was no awareness at the beginning
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה on 2a, which lists the different cases of knowing and not knowing about טומאה.

phrases.english: but there was awareness at the end" —
is there anyone who does not have
knowledge from his teacher's school?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's explanation in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that childhood learning counts as 'knowing'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone has childhood knowledge, then the משנה's case of having no knowledge at the beginning could never happen.

steps.title: A child captured among non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the case does exist: a Jewish child captured and raised among non-Jews never learned anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Yes, there is such a person. You find it in a child who was taken captive among non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his explanation. He shows a real case where a person never had any childhood knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תינוק שנשבה never went to a Jewish teacher, so he truly never knew. That makes the משנה's case of 'no awareness at the beginning' possible, and אביי's explanation still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
You can find it, meaning such a case exists
A Jewish child captured and raised among non-Jews, who never learned Jewish law

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, 'knowing' includes even the basics learned as a child. So the only person who truly never knew is someone like a תינוק שנשבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The תינוק שנשבה is a standard example throughout the תלמוד of someone with no Jewish knowledge at all.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
you find it
in a child who was taken captive among the non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a real example that fits the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone has childhood knowledge, so the משנה's case is impossible
steps.terutzMaskana: A captured child truly never knew, so the case exists

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה about carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of our משנה: carrying out on שבת is 'two that are four.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Acts of carrying out on שבת are two that are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of our משנה. This sets up the comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists several 'two that are four' cases, and carrying on שבת is one of them. The גמרא will now ask why this wording is shorter than the wording in מסכת שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts of carrying an item from one domain to another on Shabbat
Two that are four: two basic types that split into four cases

phrases.english: Acts of carrying out on Shabbat:
two that are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying out on Shabbat is described as 'two that are four'

steps.title: Why is this משנה shorter than the one in שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the fuller wording of the משנה in מסכת שבת and asks why our משנה says only 'two that are four.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: Acts of carrying out on שבת are two that are four inside, and two that are four outside. What is different here, that the משנה says only 'two that are four' and nothing more? And what is different there, that it says 'two that are four inside and two that are four outside'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the parallel משנה from מסכת שבת. It points out that it has twice as many cases, and asks why the two lists are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in שבת gives eight cases: four for bringing an item in and four for taking it out. Our משנה gives only four. The גמרא wants to know why the same topic is counted differently in the two places.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside: bringing an item into a private domain
Outside: taking an item out to a public domain
What is different? A question asking why two cases are treated differently
And nothing more

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is the very first משנה of מסכת שבת (2a).

phrases.english: Acts of carrying out on Shabbat:
two that are four inside,
and two that are four outside.
What is different here
that it teaches "two that are four" and nothing more,
and what is different there, that it teaches
"two that are four inside
and two that are four outside"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the line just quoted with the parallel משנה in שבת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does our משנה list fewer carrying cases than the משנה in שבת?

steps.title: Main categories here, sub-categories only in מסכת שבת
steps.stepSummary: מסכת שבת is the main place for the laws of שבת, so it lists main and sub-categories. שבועות lists only the main categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in מסכת שבת, which is the main place for the laws of שבת, the משנה teaches both main categories and sub-categories. Here, which is not the main place for the laws of שבת, the משנה teaches the main categories but not the sub-categories.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Each משנה gives the amount of detail that fits its location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת שבת is the home of the laws of שבת, so it gives the full picture. Our משנה mentions שבת only in passing, so it gives just the main categories (אבות) and leaves out the sub-categories (תולדות). That is why our list is half as long.

keyTerms.meaning: Main categories
Sub-categories that branch off the main ones
The main place where the laws of Shabbat are taught

phrases.english: There, which is the main place of Shabbat,
it teaches main categories and sub-categories.
Here, which is not the main place of Shabbat,
it teaches the main categories,
and it does not teach the sub-categories.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה lists only the main categories because שבועות is not the main place for Shabbat laws

steps.title: Carrying out gives only two, not four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if the main categories are only acts of carrying out, there are only two of them, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the main categories? Acts of carrying out. But acts of carrying out are only two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If our משנה lists only main categories, the count does not reach four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main categories are acts of taking an item out from a private domain to a public one. That gives only two cases. So how can our משנה say 'two that are four'? The next step rejects one possible way out. Then רב פפא gives a new answer in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they?
They are only two

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is challenging its own answer from step 20, because 'main categories only' seems to leave just two cases.

phrases.english: What are the main categories?
Acts of carrying out.
But acts of carrying out are only two!
phrases.notes: The two are: the person inside the house takes the item out, or the person outside reaches in and takes it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה lists only the main categories
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The main categories are only acts of carrying out, which come to two. That does not match the משנה's 'four.'

steps.title: Ruling out a mix of liable and exempt cases
steps.stepSummary: One might say the four cases include two liable and two exempt. But the משנה lists this like מראות נגעים, where all four count fully, so all four here must be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: some of the four cases bring liability and some are exempt. But the משנה lists this the same way as the shades of נגעים. Just as there all four count fully, so too here all four must bring liability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible way out of the last question and then rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way out would be: the 'four' are two liable cases plus two exempt ones. This fails because our משנה lists carrying out together with מראות נגעים, and there all four shades count fully. So the 'four' here must all be cases of liability, and the question from Step 21 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings up a possible answer, usually to reject it)
Liability, being obligated (for example, to bring a קרבן)
Exempt, not liable
The shades or appearances of צרעת marks
Similar to, in the same pattern as

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the גמרא's real answer. It raises a possible answer only to show it does not work. The real answer comes in the next step with the word אלא.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
some of them are for liability and some of them are for exemption;
but it teaches it like the shades of leprous marks!
phrases.notes: Our משנה also says the shades of נגעים are 'two that are four,' in the same list.

phrases.english: Just as there, all of them are for liability,
so too here, all of them are for liability!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מֵהֶן לְחִיּוּב וּמֵהֶן לִפְטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible defense against the question in Step 21, so that question stands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the four cases of carrying out include exempt cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה lists carrying out alongside מראות נגעים, where all four count fully. Listing things side by side means they follow the same pattern, so all four here must be liable.

steps.title: רב פפא: here only the liable cases are listed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. מסכת שבת, the main place for שבת laws, lists both liable and exempt cases. Our משנה lists only the liable ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: There, in מסכת שבת, the main place for the laws of שבת, the משנה lists both liable cases and exempt cases. Here, the משנה lists only the liable cases and not the exempt ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא replaces the answer from Step 20 with a different reason why the two משניות count differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the difference was main categories against sub-categories. רב פפא says the difference is liable against exempt. מסכת שבת's longer list includes exempt cases. Our משנה cuts those out and keeps only the four liable cases, which fits the comparison to מראות נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
The main place where the laws of שבת are taught (מסכת שבת)
Cases of liability and cases of exemption

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
There, which is the main place of Shabbat,
it teaches cases of liability and cases of exemption;
here, it teaches the cases of liability
and does not teach the cases of exemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the earlier answer was challenged and the possible defense was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explains how the two משניות differ in what they choose to list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was main categories against sub-categories (Step 20).
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is liable against exempt cases. שבועות lists only the liable ones.

steps.title: The liable cases are carrying out, but there are only two
steps.stepSummary: The liable cases are acts of carrying out. But there seem to be only two of those, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the liable cases? Acts of carrying out. But acts of carrying out are only two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the liable cases and then challenges רב פפא's answer with a counting problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the liable cases are only acts of carrying out from a private area to a public one, there seem to be just two of them. So how can our משנה call them 'four'?

keyTerms.meaning: What are they?
Acts of carrying out (taking an item out of a domain)
Two

phrases.english: What are the cases of liability? Acts of carrying out;
but acts of carrying out are only two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer by counting the liable cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the 'four' are all liable cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only two acts of carrying out bring liability, so the number four does not fit.

steps.title: Two of carrying out and two of bringing in
steps.stepSummary: The four liable cases are two acts of carrying out and two acts of bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two of carrying out and two of bringing in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the counting problem: bringing an item in from the public area also counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking an item from private to public is one direction. Bringing an item from public to private is the other. Each direction has two liable cases, which makes four.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out (from a private domain to a public domain)
Bringing in (from a public domain to a private domain)

phrases.english: Two of carrying out and two of bringing in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem from Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds the other direction (bringing in) to reach four.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only carrying out counts, which gives just two cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two cases of carrying out plus two of bringing in make four.

steps.title: But the משנה says only 'carrying out'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the word 'carrying out' and does not mention bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'acts of carrying out'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on counting bringing in as part of the four. But the משנה says only 'carrying out,' so how can bringing in be included?

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches (introduces a challenge from the exact words of a source)

phrases.english: But it teaches "acts of carrying out"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 25 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that bringing in is part of the four cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word is 'carrying out,' which seems to leave out bringing in.

steps.title: רב אשי: the תנא calls bringing in 'carrying out' too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the תנא uses the word 'carrying out' for bringing in as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The תנא also calls bringing in 'carrying out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the wording problem by explaining how the תנא uses the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא, 'carrying out' is a general word for moving an item from one domain to another, in either direction. So the משנה's word 'carrying out' already covers bringing in.

keyTerms.meaning: The author of the משנה
He calls it

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The tanna, bringing in as well,
he calls it "carrying out."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: תַּנָּא, הַכְנָסָה נָמֵי ״הוֹצָאָה״ קָרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the תנא uses the word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Carrying out' means only taking an item out to the public domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא's word 'carrying out' includes bringing in.

steps.title: Asking for proof of רב אשי's claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the תנא calls bringing in 'carrying out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב אשי's claim. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer depends on how the תנא uses words, so the גמרא wants proof from another משנה. The proof itself comes in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (a request for proof)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of רב אשי's answer in Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the תנא calls bringing in 'carrying out.'
